Line three, Tuesday night.
The industrial PC still runs. But something inside it has started to fail.
No alarm yet.
A PCIe link reports errors. A disk wears down. One app crashes again and again.
Windows logs every one of them. Nobody looks.
Then the line stops.
A technician drives out, opens the event viewer, and starts guessing.
What if the PC could read those logs itself?
That is the idea behind Greenforest.
Greenforest is a health service that runs on the SIMATIC IPC.
Every thirty seconds, it takes the pulse of the machine.
It needs no extra drivers and no internet connection.
It reads what Windows already collects: the event log, performance counters, NVMe SMART and the BIOS sensors.
The result is a score for eleven parts of the PC.
Disks, temperature and fans, memory, platform, drivers, stability, software and network.
Each part shows one of four NAMUR NE 107 states.
Normal. Maintenance required. Off spec. Failure.
A small anomaly model learns how this particular PC behaves on a good day.
It runs on the Intel NPU, the AI block built into the processor.
One check takes a quarter of a millisecond.
The whole service uses about a quarter of a percent of a single core.
Production software keeps the processor to itself.
You can test that yourself: the dashboard has an NPU load test.
It ran forty-one thousand inferences in ten seconds, and the NPU graph climbed.
On the first test PC, Greenforest found a real fault.
More than twelve thousand corrected hardware errors, almost all from one PCIe port in front of the Samsung SSD.
Every finding comes with its evidence.
Click it, and you see each record: time, device, error code and the full log entry.
Is the problem already known?
Acknowledge it with a reason, your name and an expiry date.
From then on, it no longer lowers the score.
If it gets worse, it is raised again. A failure always stays visible.
The plant can read the health as JSON or over OPC UA.
Encrypted, with a login, and switched off until an administrator enables it.
On the IPC itself, a dashboard shows every value and every finding.
One click from the score to the cause.
Today, Greenforest runs on one PC.
Next comes every IPC in the plant: trained centrally, checked locally, each on its own NPU.
Nineteen sources. Eleven components. One NPU.
Not a single log read by hand.
Greenforest.
An industrial PC that tells you how it is doing.
Before the line stops.
Stay green.
